name: format_synapse_message off main
summary: F4 off-main formatting mechanism SHIPPED + PROVEN. New Qt-free async_format.py (single-consumer FIFO) runs the pure format_synapse_message off the Qt thread; only insertHtml crosses back on main. chat_display.py integrates it with a public opt-in (enable_off_main_format). Proven off-main + FIFO ordering + byte-equal under stock Python AND at the live H22.0.400 seat via hython offscreen. Ships OFF BY DEFAULT (append_synapse_message keeps its synchronous contract; zero default-behaviour change; panel slice floor unchanged). The one-line PANEL ACTIVATION lives in synapse_panel._on_done -- W2-S5's OPEN claim on synapse_panel.py -- and is the recorded blocked remainder.

findings.claim: F4 mechanism shipped as a Qt-free single-consumer FIFO (async_format.py). Ordering is correct BY CONSTRUCTION (a single serial consumer cannot reorder). Qt objects never cross to the worker: a job carries plain data in and an HTML string out; the caller owns the one Qt hop (a queued signal that wakes the main-thread drain). This satisfies crucible criterion 1 (prerendered HTML strings only cross back).

Off-main is OFF BY DEFAULT. Making append_synapse_message async-by-default breaks two existing tests that read the document synchronously right after appending: test_chat_panel::test_append_synapse_message and test_panel_faces::test_synapse_reply_carries_signed_author. The second is in W2-S5's CLAIMED file (test_panel_faces.py), so it cannot be adapted here. Default-off preserves the synchronous contract, holds the floor, and makes the whole change a pure addition with zero default-behaviour change. The panel opts in via chat.enable_off_main_format() -- a one-line call whose home is synapse_panel._on_done / panel init, i.e. the S5-blocked synapse_panel.py.

UX finding for Joe (recorded, NOT changed): set_max_result_blocks caps QTextDocument BLOCKS for an O(1) relayout bound, but a single chat message spans several blocks, so a block cap can clip the OLDEST MESSAGE mid-body. Whole-message trimming (trim on message boundaries, not blocks) is the correct UX. Enabling trimming and picking the cap is Joe's decision; this leg leaves the default UNLIMITED, pinned by test_chatdisplay_trimming_default_unchanged.

Telemetry stays honest and does not drift in the default path. The DEFAULT (sync) append records exactly ONE 'append' phase sample (format+insert together, on-main) like base. When off-main is enabled, the format is timed as an OFF-MAIN 'append' sample (record_result_phase derives thread identity) and the insert as an ON-MAIN 'append' sample -- the two buckets never mix, which is precisely how the F4 win (the four-regex pass leaving the Qt thread) becomes visible in result_render_stats without ever being read as a main-thread stall. No edit to result_telemetry.py (not in touches; used as-is).

When off-main is ENABLED, the streaming finalize (end_stream) removes the streamed plain text on main (sync) then defers the formatted insert -- a brief flicker in place of the old main-thread freeze while a huge reply formats. This is strictly the intended trade (GUI stays responsive), only occurs when the panel opts in, and never in the default state. Not a blocker; noted for the panel-activation reviewer.
